mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting central bank tightening that suppresses equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) indicate a tightening monetary cycle that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime with unemployment below 4.0% and strong job growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 100k), corporate earnings rise, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS MoM > 100k.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand and economic confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (index, 2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is below 2.0% annualized and housing starts (HOUST) decline month-over-month, it indicates economic weakness that suppresses equity returns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both GDPC1 < 2.0% and HOUST MoM < 0.

mechanism_narrative: In a recessionary phase with unemployment above 6.0% and weak job growth (PAYEMS monthly change < 50k), central bank easing policies boost equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0 and PAYEMS MoM < 50k.
